chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hammam, from Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a man who had incurred the Hadd penalty, and he had numerous sores on his body. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Delay it until he is cured. Do not peel them off him, lest you kill him.'

key_terms.تَنْكَئُوهَا: you peel them off (cause them to bleed/wound)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on delaying Hadd punishment for an ill person?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delayed the execution of the Hadd penalty for a man covered in sores, instructing officials not to aggravate his wounds to prevent death. This incident highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship), demonstrating that the severity of the punishment must be proportionate to the offender's physical capacity to endure it. It serves as a foundational precedent for considering medical conditions and injury severity when applying corporal punishments in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Hammam, from Muhammad Bin Saeed, from Al Sakuny, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘They came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> with a man who had numerous sores in his body. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Delay it until he is cured. Do not peel these off (by beating him) for you would kill him’.
